quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: Dominion Energy Virginia 2025 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy Virginia 2025 IRP Update - data center contracts: as of July 31, 2025 the company had 16,913 MW of requested data center capacity under firm contracts (executed Electric Service Agreements or Construction Letters of Authorization) and was studying an additional 30,132 MW at the Engineering Letter of Authorization stage. ESAs grew from 5,827 MW (end of July 2023) to 8,012 MW (2024) and 9,815 MW (2025); CLOAs from 2,008 MW to 5,835 MW and 7,098 MW. Connections: six new data center campuses connected in 2025 as of October 1 with an ultimate capacity of 456 MW, and the company expected 8 new campus connects with an ultimate capacity of 561 MW in 2025 (2024: 15 campuses, 977 MW; on average 15 campuses a year since 2013). The company says data centers have so far been hesitant to participate in demand response or interruptible service programs.
quarterly_data.figure: 16,913 MW under ESAs/CLOAs (July 31, 2025): ESAs 9,815 MW, CLOAs 7,098 MW; 30,132 MW at ELOA stage; 2025 connects 6 campuses / 456 MW (8 / 561 MW expected); 2024 15 campuses / 977 MW

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: Dominion Energy Virginia 2025 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy Virginia 2025 IRP Update - load forecast and build plan: demand in the DOM Zone is forecasted to increase 6.3% annually over the next decade and more than double by 2045; under the 2025 PJM Load Forecast the DOM Zone 20-year CAGR is 4.1% for coincident peak and 5.3% for energy, and increases in the data center load forecast remain a key driver of the year-over-year forecast changes. The DOM Zone set an all-time record peak of 24,678 MW on January 23, 2025. The Company Preferred Plan (PJM Derived Load Forecast) includes 17,534 MW of solar, 3,460 MW of wind, 2,000 MW of storage, 1,944 MW of nuclear and 8,510 MW of natural gas-fired generation over the 2026-2045 planning period (NPV total $148.7B); the company says natural gas generation will be a critical component of reliably meeting demand.
quarterly_data.figure: DOM Zone demand +6.3% annually over next decade, more than double by 2045; record peak 24,678 MW; Preferred Plan: 8,510 MW gas, 17,534 MW solar, 3,460 MW wind, 2,000 MW storage, 1,944 MW nuclear
